jd:
Our Commitment to Students

At Canadian Tire, we are committed to providing students with a supportive and collaborative environment that fosters knowledge sharing and offers key experiences to help them develop their capabilities through projects and objectives. We believe in setting specific and measurable goals that align with our business objectives to support learning and help students achieve their full potential. Our culture emphasizes learning from others, continuous improvement, agility, growth, and innovation, and we are invested in building a talented, diverse workforce for the future of Canada and Canadian Tire. Additionally, we are dedicated to building strong relationships with our student employees by engaging with them throughout their education and career pursuits and creating opportunities for ongoing communication and relationship building.

Are you excited about building software and transforming AI ideas into secure, scalable enterprise solutions?

Join our Engineering Practices team and help build AI-enabled solutions that improve productivity, knowledge sharing, engineering workflows, and employee experiences across the organization.

Working alongside engineering leaders, staff engineers, developers, and quality engineers, you may contribute to initiatives such as the CTC News Funnel, Developer Career Path Guidance Automation, AI Marketplace adoption, reusable engineering assistants, and other initiatives on our AI roadmap.

You will be encouraged to bring fresh perspectives, experiment with emerging technologies, and help progress promising ideas from proof-of-concepts to scalable minimum viable products.

What You’ll Do



- Research and propose AI opportunities that address real engineering and organizational needs. 
- Design, code, test, and refine AI-enabled applications, integrations, and automations. 
- Apply software engineering fundamentals to build secure, maintainable, and scalable solutions. 
- Work with programming languages, frameworks, APIs, data sources, automation tools, and AI technologies. 
- Help grow AI Marketplace adoption by contributing reusable solutions, coding agents, workflows, prompts, and developer accelerators. 
- Gather feedback from users and technical stakeholders to improve solutions. 
- Create clear technical guidance, examples, diagrams, and demonstrations. 
- Participate in Communities of Practice, workshops, and solution showcases. 
- Evaluate solutions for business value, technical feasibility, security, scalability, and responsible AI considerations. 

What We’re Looking For



- Currently enrolled in a post-secondary program in computer science, software engineering, computer engineering, artificial intelligence, data science, information technology, or a related field. 
- Demonstrated programming ability and a solid understanding of software development fundamentals. 
- Ability to independently write, debug, test, and explain code. 
- Ability to critically review and validate code rather than relying solely on AI-generated output. 
- Hands-on development experience gained through coursework, personal projects, hackathons, internships, or open-source contributions. 
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills. 
- Curiosity, creativity, and a willingness to explore unfamiliar technologies and propose new ideas. 

Technical Skills

Experience in some of the following areas would be an asset:



- Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Swift, Python, Kotlin, Node.js, React, or Dart. 
- Git and GitHub. 
- APIs, scripting, automation, application integration, and data processing. 
- Testing, debugging, error handling, code review, and continuous integration. 
- Software architecture and Software Development Life Cycle fundamentals. 
- Markdown, Mermaid, Confluence, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365. 

AI-Assisted Development

Experience with developer-assistance tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or similar coding-focused tools would be an asset.

AI tools should accelerate your work, not replace your engineering judgment. You should be able to understand, test, explain, and correct AI-generated code while considering functionality, security, privacy, quality, and maintainability.

What You’ll Gain



- Hands-on experience building AI-enabled solutions in an enterprise engineering environment. 
- Opportunities to bring forward original ideas and turn them into working solutions. 
- Practical experience taking solutions from proof-of-concepts toward scalable MVPs. 
- Exposure to enterprise architecture, security, scalability, and responsible AI. 
- Experience contributing to AI Marketplace growth, solution reuse, and adoption. 
- Opportunities to collaborate with engineering leaders, staff engineers, developers, quality engineers, and Communities of Practice. 
- Experience presenting solutions, gathering feedback, and preparing them for broader organizational use. 

Application and Interview Expectations 

Candidates should be prepared to discuss a project they have built, walk through their code and technical decisions, and explain how they tested and validated the solution, including any use of AI-assisted developer tools.

Skills

The interview process will assess foundational coding and software development skills. While it may not include a live coding exercise, candidates should be prepared to:



- Demonstrate an understanding of core programming concepts. 
- Read and reason about code. 
- Explain expected code behaviour. 
- Identify potential issues or defects. 
- Describe how they would test, debug, or improve a solution. 

Experience with AI-assisted development is welcome, but candidates must be able to understand, verify, and explain the code they submit or discuss.

We’re always looking for great talent! In addition to competitive pay, we offer:



- Career growth opportunities and product discounts

Broadband Salary Range: $23.00– $37.00.

Our typical hiring range is between $23.00 and $30.00 CAD Hourly. Salary decisions are also dependent on other factors such as your experience, job-related knowledge, skills and competencies, market location, industry benchmarks, internal equity and other role-specific requirements.

This posting represents an existing vacancy within our organization.

We may use artificial intelligence tools as part of our recruitment process to assist in the initial screening of resumes. All hiring decisions, including candidate evaluation, selection, and disposition, are made by human recruiters.

About Us

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most admired and trusted companies. With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. We offer competitive salaries and wages to CTC employees, as well as store discounts, supported learning through our Triangle Learning Academy, Canadian Tire Profit Sharing, and retirement and savings programs for eligible employees. As part of our enhanced flex benefits program, we offer mental health benefits in the amount of $5,000 per year for benefits-eligible employees and their families, including total well-being, and mental health tools and resources for all employees. Join us in helping to make life in Canada better through living and working our Core Values: we are innovators and entrepreneurs at our core, outcomes drive us, inclusion is a must, we are stronger together and we take personal responsibility. It is an especially exciting time to join CTC and its family of companies where career opportunities are wide-ranging! Join us, where there's a place for you here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

We are committed to fostering an environment where belonging thrives, and diversity, inclusion and equity are infused into everything we do. We believe in building an organizational culture where people are consistently treated with dignity while respecting individual religion, nationality, gender, race, age, perceived ability, spoken language, sexual orientation, and identification. We are united in our purpose of being here to help make life in Canada better.

Accommodations 

We stand firm in our Core Value that inclusion is a must. We welcome and encourage candidates from equity-seeking groups such as people who identify as racialized, Indigenous, 2SLGBTQIA+, women, people with disabilities, and beyond. Should you require any accommodation in applying for this role, or throughout the interview process, please make them known when contacted and we will work with you to help meet your needs.

role: 2027 Spring Internship: Vehicle Software Integration Engineer
jd:
Company Information
PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture and customer support of high-quality light-, medium- and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates. PACCAR also designs and manufactures advanced power trains, provides financial services and information technology, and distributes truck parts related to its principal business.


Requisition Summary
PACCAR Innovation Center has an internship for students currently enrolled in college. This opening is for a Vehicle Software Integration Engineer Intern to add to our Innovation team in Silicon Valley, California.
This is an on-site internship, expected to start in January 2027 and continue through May 2027, with the possibility of extending beyond May based on availability.


Job Responsibilities
You will join PACCAR's Silicon Valley Innovation team, which explores emerging, state-of-the-art vehicle technologies to keep our trucks at the forefront of innovation.
 
This is a hands-on role. You will build real systems and show the results in a working Class 8 semi-truck. You will work on a next-generation connected vehicle platform made up of three systems: a digital cockpit, a vehicle gateway and a telematics unit. Your job is to take this platform from the lab bench and integrate it into a truck. The work includes, but is not limited to:
· Studying the truck's electrical, electronic and software systems and overall vehicle architecture to understand how the new platform must fit into it.
· Identifying the hardware and software changes needed for integration, then putting them in place.
· Installing the platform in the truck, bringing it up, and validating it.
· Debugging issues across hardware, software, and vehicle networks.
· Identifying technical risks early and proposing smart ways to mitigate them early in the program.
· Coming up with creative solutions when standard approaches don't work.
· Documenting your work and demonstrating the results to engineers and leadership.
 
This role suits someone with strong problem-solving skills who enjoys hands-on engineering. If you love challenges, this is for you.


Required Qualifications
The candidate we seek will be currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechatronics, Automotive Engineering, or a related program, and will have:
· Strong understanding of vehicle systems and how they work together
· Strong understanding of vehicle networking protocols, such as CAN, automotive Ethernet and service-oriented communication (SOME/IP, DDS) or similar
· Programming and debugging in C/C++, Java or Kotlin; scripting in Python or shell
· Comfort with Linux: command line, Git, building and cross-compiling software
· Foundational understanding of vehicle electrical power and grounding, and the ability to read schematics and wiring diagrams
· Hands-on project experience bringing hardware and software together
· Operating-system fundamentals


Preferred Qualifications
The qualifications and skills that are important to be successful in this position are as follows:
· Hands-on experience with CAN, SAE J1939, DBC files, SocketCAN and tools such as CANoe, Kvaser or PCAN
· Hands-on experience with automotive Ethernet, Ethernet switches and VLANs, NAT/firewall, Wireshark or tcpdump
· Experience with real-time operating systems and platforms such as QNX or AUTOSAR, and with hypervisors (QNX Hypervisor, Xen or similar)
· Android or Android Automotive development (Java or Kotlin), ADB/fastboot, Vehicle HAL
· Embedded Linux and Yocto, bootloaders or device trees
· Hands-on experience with automotive development platforms, such as those from Qualcomm, NXP or Infineon, or other Arm-based platforms
· Linux-based telematics (TCU) platforms, connectivity SDKs such as Qualcomm TelSDK, AT commands or GNSS
· Display, audio or camera integration
· Truck or automotive electrical systems: 12/24 V power, ignition, harnesses and connectors
· Working-level understanding of OTA software updates or containers
 
You do not need to meet every requirement to be a successful candidate. If you have strong fundamentals, enjoy hands-on challenges and learn quickly, we encourage you to apply.


General Description of All Benefits
As a U.S. PACCAR intern, you have a full range of benefit options including:
· Competitive salary and 401k with up to a 5% company match
· Medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your family
· Paid holidays
· Flexible spending accounts (FSA) and health savings account (HSA)
· Life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance
· EAP services including wellness plans, estate planning, financial counseling and more
· Global Fortune 500 company with a wide array of growth, training, and development opportunities
· Work alongside experienced goal-oriented colleagues recognized as experts in their field


Additional Job Board Information
At PACCAR, we value talent and promote growth and development. We carefully consider numerous compensation factors including your education, training, or experience. A reasonable salary range estimate for the Vehicle Software Integration Engineer Intern is $25.00/Hour for students enrolled in an Undergraduate degree program and $30.00/Hour for students enrolled in a Graduate degree program. Additionally, this role is eligible for the full range of benefit options listed above.
 
PACCAR is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veteran/Disability corporation. Peterbilt promotes Diversity and Inclusion through mentorship, events, and affinity support groups – The Diversity Council, Peterbilt Women’s Initiative (PBWIN), Veterans Group, Peterbilt Black Organization for Leadership and Development (B.O.L.D) and Peterbilt+ (An LGBTQ support group).


Application Career Page Link: https://jobs.paccar.com/job/Sunnyvale-2027-Spring-Internship-Vehicle-Software-Integration-Engineer-CA-94089/1459888133/
fit_why: Embedded automotive integration: CAN, SOME/IP, QNX, hardware bring-up, C/C++

Software Engineer Intern - Server - User Lifecycle
jd:
ABOUT STRAVA

Strava is the app for active people. With over 200 million athletes in more than 185 countries, it’s more than tracking workouts—it’s where people make progress together, from new habits to new personal bests. No matter your sport or how you track it, Strava’s got you covered. Find your crew, crush your goals, and make every effort count. Start your journey https://www.strava.com/subscription with Strava today.

Our mission is simple: to motivate people to live their best active lives. We believe in the power of movement to connect and drive people forward.



As an Engineering Intern at Strava, you will be embedded in a team working on real projects that ship to our athletes and within the company, treated like a full-time member of the engineering team. You'll collaborate with cross functional teams that help us support and deliver to our athletes faster, while keeping them inspired and motivated.

We’ll give you experienced mentors and all the tools you need to make a meaningful impact on our product. To see examples of what past interns have contributed, read our Engineering Blog https://medium.com/strava-engineering/tagged/internships!




AVAILABLE INTERNSHIP:

Strava is looking for software engineering interns for a range of disciplines. Strava's engineering teams build and run the apps and services that millions of athletes rely on every day. Our engineers work across iOS, Android, web, and backend systems, shipping to a global community through frequent releases and experimentation, in close partnership with product, design, and data teams.

This internship will be supporting the User Lifecycle team, which helps athletes build lasting habits and connections on Strava. The team owns registration and onboarding, the home feed, streaks, recaps like Month in Sport and Year in Sport, and gamified experiences like segments and challenges, working across mobile and backend services to build, test, and ship improvements.



We follow a flexible hybrid model that requires you in our SF office four days per week.




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Ship to Millions of Athletes: Build and ship features across mobile, web, and backend services that reach athletes on the surfaces they use every day, including the home feed, onboarding and registration, and streaks.

 - Improve the First Impression: Help new athletes get set up and find value faster by working on the first-time user experience, registration, and sign-in flows, and measure the impact through A/B experiments.

 - Bring Data to Life: Work on shareable, personalized experiences like Month in Sport, connecting backend data pipelines and APIs to polished, animated client experiences.

 - Make Segments and Challenges More Engaging: Contribute to features that make leaderboards, segments, and other motivating games easier to discover and play.

 - Build for Scale and Reliability: Learn how to ship safely at scale with feature flags, monitoring, code review, and phased rollouts, and help modernize parts of a large, long-lived codebase.

 - Collaborate Across Disciplines: Partner with product managers, designers, analysts, and engineers across platforms, and learn from experienced mentors through design review, code review, and experiment readouts.




WE’RE EXCITED ABOUT YOU BECAUSE: 

 - You're eager to build features end to end, from technical design through to shipping and measuring real-world impact.

 - You have hands-on experience with at least one modern programming language (such as Kotlin, Swift, Scala, Go, or Ruby) and have built projects through coursework, internships, or personal work.

 - You have a solid grasp of computer science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented or functional design.

 - You write clean, well-testedf code and welcome feedback and mentorship as part of your growth.

 - You care about the athlete experience and think about how design, data, and performance come together in a product people use daily.

 - You bring curiosity, ask thoughtful questions, and contribute to a collaborative and inclusive team culture.

 - Bonus: experience with mobile development, REST APIs or backend services, A/B testing, or analytics.

 - Are currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, with an expected graduation date of May 2027, December 2027, May 2028 — OR – have recently completed or are currently enrolled in a coding bootcamp, technical training program, or are transitioning into software engineering through equivalent practical experience. 




THE SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM:

 - The program will be in our San Francisco, CA office with a hybrid office attendance requirement of 4 days per week

 - Housing Stipend for Summer is provided to live in SF for 3 months 

 - Length of program: 10-12 weeks (Summer 2027 roughly June through August). 

 - Working Hours: 40 hours per week 

 - This is a paid internship



We will be closing applications for this role on Fri, Nov 27 at 5:00pm PST.




WHY JOIN US?



Movement brings us together. At Strava, we’re building the world’s largest community of active people, helping them stay motivated and achieve their goals.

Our global team is passionate about making movement fun, meaningful, and accessible to everyone. Whether you’re shaping the technology, growing our community, or driving innovation, your work at Strava makes an impact.

When you join Strava, you’re not just joining a company—you’re joining a movement. If you’re ready to bring your energy, ideas, and drive, let’s build something incredible together.

Strava builds software that makes the best part of our athletes’ days even better. Just as we’re deeply committed to unlocking their potential, we’re dedicated to providing a world-class, inclusive workplace where our employees can grow and thrive, too. We’re backed by Sequoia Capital, TCV, Madrone Partners and Jackson Square Ventures, and we’re expanding in order to exceed the needs of our growing community of global athletes. Our culture reflects our community. We are continuously striving to hire and engage teammates from all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives because we know we are a stronger team together.

Strava is an equal opportunity employer. In keeping with the values of Strava, we make all employment decisions including hiring, evaluation, termination, promotional and training opportunities, without regard to race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, physical handicap, mental disability, medical condition, disability, gender or identity or expression, pregnancy or pregnancy-related condition, marital status, height and/or weight.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

 - Prototype with AI coding tools like Claude Code, and use visual mockups to collaborate with design and product

 - Learn from experienced engineers how we make tradeoffs, build maintainable systems, and test features to a high quality bar

 - Follow your features across the stack, starting on Android and going into Go, Scala, or Swift when the work takes you there, paired with teammates who know that code

 - You have hands-on experience building Android apps in Kotlin, whether through coursework, internships, or personal projects

 - You’re eager to build features end to end and put polished product design in athletes’ hands

 - You’re curious about how the whole product works, not just your platform. No iOS or backend experience needed; we’ll build those skills together.

 - You have a builder’s mindset: when the right tool doesn’t exist yet, you’re energized to create it

 - Experience with Jetpack Compose, Coroutines, or GraphQL is a plus
